gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the eufy E340 + E10 pair works only through the home's Wi-Fi network, not over a direct link: the doorbell has a 2.4 GHz-only 802.11 b/g/n radio, and eufy says only that the E10 'supports local network operation without an external internet connection'. The same sources also don't say that wiring the E340 to the house bell means losing a digital chime (eufy spec: 'Use Original Digital Chime: N') and needs 16–24 V. SwitchBot's monitor, by contrast, talks to its doorbell directly with no Wi-Fi if the two are within 5 m.
standout_why: I compared against Smart Home Perfected (cited) and the eufy E10 page (cited), plus the bundle page (cited) and WorthRated (top result). Smart Home Perfected already says SwitchBot 'works even without the internet' and gives the 5 m guidance. The cited eufy E10 page already gives the 3-minute live-view cap for battery cameras. None of these pages says how the E10 reaches the E340 (through the router, not directly), what the E340's wired voltage is, or that it can't be used with a digital chime. Smart Home Perfected says only that it 'runs on a quick release battery or on wired power'. WorthRated doesn't mention eufy, existing doorbell wiring or transformer voltage at all.
decides: This splits the two wireless cards by how the doorbell reaches the screen. If the shopper wants a screen that keeps working when the router or internet is down, or has no Wi-Fi at the door, the SwitchBot kit fits: eufy's own support page says the monitor still shows live video and two-way talk without Wi-Fi within 5 m. The eufy E10 rides on the home network. It also cuts battery-doorbell live view at 3 minutes, so the E340 should be hardwired. Hardwiring needs a 16–24 V doorbell circuit and a mechanical chime, not a digital one. For the wired 7-inch kits ChatGPT showed (Adrinfly, Aoibox), I suspect they need their own cable run from door to monitor rather than reusing the bell wire, but I could not source that (see unsourced).
